docket.challenge_claim: Two byte-checkable naming lapses: the armies fled from are Chaldean in both witnesses rather than Babylonian, and the ancestor whose charge the unit turns on stands in two attested spellings inside this span, undisclosed.
docket.grounds: The first lapse is real; the second is a true byte observation wrongly framed as a lapse of the same class, so the challenge is refined rather than upheld whole. First: oshb:Jer.35.11 reads מִפְּנֵי֙ חֵ֣יל הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וּמִפְּנֵ֖י חֵ֣יל אֲרָ֑ם (oshb:Jer.35.11, byte) -- for fear of the army of the Chaldeans and for fear of the army of Aram. The Babylon token stands once in that verse and only inside the royal title, נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֮ (oshb:Jer.35.11, byte), and the Babylon token, its directional form and the Chaldeans token are separate count objects that are never blended. Calling the armies Babylonian blends two of them at the single place in the span where the distinction is visible, and both witnesses read otherwise: “for fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians” (web:Jer.35.11). Second: the ancestor does stand in two attested spellings in span -- the short form יוֹנָדָ֨ב (oshb:Jer.35.6, byte), which sweeps to 3 verses at the consonantal tier (oshb:Jer.35.6, oshb:Jer.35.10, oshb:Jer.35.19), and the long form יְהוֹנָדָ֤ב (oshb:Jer.35.8, byte), which sweeps to 4 (oshb:Jer.35.8, oshb:Jer.35.14, oshb:Jer.35.16, oshb:Jer.35.18), both confined to this chapter. But the duty to name a name form is triggered by a digit, a form claim or an exclusivity claim about the name, and this row hangs none: it quotes the ancestor inside a verse splice and counts nothing. Recording the variance would improve the row; its absence is not a defect, and pairing it with the token blend overstates it. Neither item moves a boundary: the header at oshb:Jer.35.1 is a byte-identical member of the prose-sermon superscription shape, the closing seam rests on the verse-initial word-event onset at oshb:Jer.35.12, and the span's marks -- the preceding petuchah at oshb:Jer.34.22, the closing petuchah at oshb:Jer.35.11 and the count-only paseq at oshb:Jer.35.5 -- all match the inventory (single-witness WLC), with no variant note owed anywhere in the span.

MT 21:1 carries פַּשְׁחוּר֙ בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.21.1, byte) and MT 38:1 carries וּפַשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte) - the same name-plus-patronymic pair - so the full patronymic joins those two sites rather than separating them, and the chapter-20 priest the note names instead is not the collision. Conversely the embassy member stands as יְהוּכַ֣ל בֶּן שֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.37.3, byte) against וְיוּכַל֙ בֶּן שֶׁ֣לֶמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), where both elements differ in form, so full-patronymic matching would split one man. The unit also splices two different spellings of the Malchiah name into one row under one English name with no spelling disclosure: מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte) against מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.6, byte), the second the only such form of that name in the book (sweep: 1 verse) - the exact site the per-attested-spelling rule targets. Frame ownership: two koh-amar frames stand in span, כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.38.2, byte) and כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.3, byte). Neither is quoted, the splice offered beginning after the first; the second goes unmentioned; and the declared koh-amar signal therefore rests on no quoted form. The mouth sentence attached to the splice names Yahweh as the formula's mouth, where MT 38:1 reads אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל כָּל הָעָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), making these the words Jeremiah was speaking to all the people. One refinement of the framing that does not change the outcome: a clause earlier in the same field does say that what the officials heard is Jeremiah's own proclamation, so the defect is a contradictory mouth attribution in one sentence rather than a wholly unnamed mouth, and the cure is a clause rather than a rebuild. One finding outside the challenge as raised, byte-verified: three paseq segs stand inside Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6, two keyed to MT 38:4 and one to MT 38:6 (single-witness, count-only), and the unit discloses no paseq at all, although the units on either side of it in this material do disclose that layer. The three parashah marks it cites, at MT 38:1, MT 38:2 and MT 38:6, are correct under their own type, and the ketiv/qere at MT 38:2 is correctly disclosed and correctly scoped, the splice ending before the pair.
docket.remedy: device_notes: replace the full-patronymic sentence with the per-site reading the bytes give - name MT 21:1 as the site the full patronymic joins rather than separates, and disclose the two Malchiah spellings the unit itself splices, מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה at MT 38:1 against מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ at MT 38:6, with a digit naming the swept object and unit; add the in-span paseq disclosure for MT 38:4 and MT 38:6, single-witness, count-only, no position claimed. boundary_rationale: quote the koh-amar form at MT 38:2 rather than beginning the splice after it, add the second frame at MT 38:3, and re-word the mouth sentence so the formula's mouth is named as Jeremiah relaying it to all the people. Tests the cure must pass: every name form claimed is quoted at its own site in its attested spelling with the count object named before the digit; every declared speech_formula signal has a quoted form standing behind it; every koh-amar citation names whose mouth carries it; every apparatus class present in Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6 disclosed.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A new set of four named officials opens the span, וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע שְׁפַטְיָ֣ה בֶן מַתָּ֗ן וּגְדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן פַּשְׁח֔וּר וְיוּכַל֙ בֶּן שֶׁ֣לֶמְיָ֔הוּ וּפַשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה אֶ֨ת הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל כָּל הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), matching “Shephatiah the son of Mattan, Gedaliah the son of Pashhur, Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur the son of Malchijah heard the words that Jeremiah spoke to all the people, saying,” (web:Jer.38.1); a setumah marks this same verse, oshb:Jer.38.1 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration). What they heard is Jeremiah's own proclamation to the people, opening הַיֹּשֵׁב֙ בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את יָמ֕וּת בַּחֶ֖רֶב בָּרָעָ֣ב וּבַדָּ֑בֶר (oshb:Jer.38.2, byte; a ketiv/qere note also sits later in this verse, not engaged by this splice) — matching “He who remains in this city will die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence,” (web:Jer.38.2) — the divine formula naming Yahweh as its mouth; a further setumah falls at this same verse, oshb:Jer.38.2. The officials petition the king that Jeremiah be put to death for weakening the soldiers' resolve, matching “Then the princes said to the king, "Please let this man be put to death, because he weakens the hands of the men of war who remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, in speaking such words to them; for this man doesn't seek the welfare of this people, but harm."” (web:Jer.38.4); Zedekiah answers that he is in their hand, matching “Zedekiah the king said, "Behold, he is in your hand; for the king can't do anything to oppose you."” (web:Jer.38.5), and they cast him into Malchijah's cistern, וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֨כוּ אֹת֜וֹ אֶל הַבּ֣וֹר מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ בֶן הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר֙ בַּחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָ֔ה וַיְשַׁלְּח֥וּ אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בַּחֲבָלִ֑ים וּבַבּ֤וֹר אֵֽין מַ֨יִם֙ כִּ֣י אִם טִ֔יט וַיִּטְבַּ֥ע יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בַּטִּֽיט (oshb:Jer.38.6, byte), where a third setumah closes the span at this same verse, oshb:Jer.38.6 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration).

He is likely to die in the place where he is, because of the famine; for there is no more bread in the city."” (web:Jer.38.9) — opening אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.38.9, byte), the same human vocative used of Zedekiah earlier in these chapters rather than a divine title — and the king commands the rescue, וַיְצַוֶּ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֛ת עֶֽבֶד מֶ֥לֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר קַ֣ח בְּיָדְךָ֤ מִזֶּה֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְֽהַעֲלִ֜יתָ אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֧הוּ הַנָּבִ֛יא מִן הַבּ֖וֹר בְּטֶ֥רֶם יָמֽוּת (oshb:Jer.38.10, byte). docket.challenge_claim: The divine-title claim at 38:17 has no support in the form the unit quotes, blends distinct count objects, and asserts an in-chapter recurrence the bytes do not contain; a cited K/Q verse is also left undisclosed.
docket.grounds: All four limbs verify, and the first is worse at the bytes than as raised. The device-note run is צִדְקִיָּ֡הוּ כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֩ (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte). It is called the full title stack, yet it carries no title element at all: the stack stands next in the verse as אֱלֹהֵ֨י צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte). The run is non-parallel to its paired rendering at both ends - it opens on the addressee's name, which the rendering does not carry, and it stops before the three-word title the rendering does carry - so the mandatory engagement on a boundary-relevant title claim rests on a splice containing none of it. The object is blended. The form present is the Elohei-tsevaot Elohei-Yisrael stack (sweep: 3 verses - 35:17, 38:17, 44:7), a different count object from the book's signature stack (sweep: 32 verses), of which 38:17 is not a member: swept from the signature form as it stands at MT 39:16, the 32 verses are returned without 38:17 among them. The recurrence claim is false at the bytes: of the 3 verses carrying the form, exactly 1 falls in chapters 37-38, namely 38:17 itself, so the assertion that the same full stack is used elsewhere in these chapters has no site to point to, and it is made with no digit and no swept object. A tier label on the splice does not stand in for a recurrence check. Ketiv/qere: one note stands at MT 38:16, a verse the unit cites for its mark and characterises as the king's sworn oath, with the pair inside that oath clause, חַי יְהוָ֞ה את אֲשֶׁר֩ (oshb:Jer.38.16, byte; single-witness apparatus); no disclosure appears. High severity is right: this is not a wording matter but a title claim, a count object and a recurrence all unsupported at the bytes, in the field where the unit's one declared speech-formula signal is argued. What holds: the parashah marks keyed to MT 38:13, MT 38:16, MT 38:18 and MT 38:19 all match under their own types with the two types never conflated, and the mouth of the oracle is correctly named as Jeremiah's rather than left to the formula. Two findings outside the challenge as raised. A paseq seg stands at MT 38:20, inside Jer.38.14-Jer.38.20 (single-witness, count-only), undisclosed. And the supporting reading offered elsewhere for this unit - that the fuller stack is correctly distinguished from the shorter form used earlier in this narrative - answers a claim the unit does not make: the unit's sentence asserts that the same full stack recurs in these chapters, and that is the sentence the bytes refute.

A note that carries no evidentiary force cannot generate an omission defect elsewhere, and the item cites no bytes and no ref for the duty it asserts. What is defective in the very field the item points at is adjacent and checkable: device_notes argues that the guard-captain's title is carried forward by 'the following span', a positional cross-reference, where the title in fact stands as רַב טַבָּחִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.39.11, byte) and again at oshb:Jer.39.13, neither of which appears in boundary_evidence_refs, though that field does carry oshb:Jer.39.7 for the front seam. A verse argued in prose outside the row's own span belongs in the refs, and a cross-row reference is verse-anchored, not positional. Second, undetected by either item: the quotation of web:Jer.39.8 in boundary_rationale renders the staged text's two right single quotation marks as straight typewriter apostrophes, in 'king's' and in 'people's' - the straight-for-curly class; the unit's other two renderings, of web:Jer.39.9 and web:Jer.39.10, are character-exact against the staged text. docket.grounds: The word-event item is upheld and can be put more sharply. Of the three counted shapes (21, 11 and 4 verses) exactly one, the narrative-onset shape, is verb-initial (1 of 3). The superscription shape opens with the article-noun and stands its verb third - הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה (oshb:Jer.40.1, byte) - and the topical-header shape opens with the relative particle; the counted inventory further separates the three as different unit classes, narrative onset against prose-sermon superscription against topical header, so calling them 'the book's two counted narrative shapes' both undercounts the system and mis-classes the shape it names. The non-membership finding survives intact: 39:15 fronts a prepositional addressee phrase ahead of the verb - וְאֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הָיָ֣ה דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.39.15, byte) - and belongs to none of the three. The form-label is also wrong: that fronted element is not the object, and the clause subject is the word-of-YHWH phrase itself. The declared-signal item is upheld and extends further than stated: the full signature title stack stands at כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.39.16, byte) and is never quoted, tier-labelled or mouth-named, and the unit's rendering of that verse is cut with an inserted ellipsis - a character the staged text does not carry - at exactly the point where the staged rendering goes on to render that stack, so the sole speech-formula entry among this unit's 2 declared signals loses its evidence in both languages at once. The closure token does stand at MT 39:17 and MT 39:18 (2 verses in span), unnamed; at 162 verses book-wide it is closure corroboration only, so that is under-engagement, not a missing driver. The quote-fidelity item is upheld and under-counted: the rendering of web:Jer.39.18 degrades four marks, not two - the contraction in 'won't', the mark closing the embedded clause after 'trust in me,', and both marks in the trailing pair after 'says Yahweh' - and a fifth degraded mark stands in the rendering of web:Jer.39.15, in 'Yahweh's', which no item names. The resumption point is refuted as a defect: the pre-fall setting argues for this cut rather than against it, and the disclosed cohesion duty runs to byte-true devices straddling the seam that argue continuity against the row, so its absence is an unused corroboration, not an omission. Confirmed sound: the ketiv/qere note at MT 39:16 is disclosed present-but-not-engaged and correctly scoped, since the rendering stops before it, and the setumah marks at MT 39:14 and MT 39:18 verify under their own type.
